items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: And then you brought Rick [Montalbano] into the band, is that right?

ctx.x: did manage to hook up with a percussionist, Don Alias, who had lots of good connections in the jazz industry as well as the basic music industry, and he got him together with Bobby Colomby, the producer for Blood, Sweat and Tears, and so that’s how the first Jaco album actually came to be. So in a way I kind of pat myself on the back by saying hey, I mean Don Alias was on my gig and they knew each other, but once they were in the same band things get tighter. And so as a result of that, I think Jaco’s story kind…

Yeah. It’s nice to be part of his story in a positive way. And I forgot that you had Don Alias on that gig. He was a great guy too. And then you brought Rick [Montalbano] into the band, is that right?

Yeah, that was my first official act. When the piano player/conductor left and they said okay they want to make you the musical director, of course we’ve got to find a piano player. And I said “got the guy.”
